sections.sectionSummaryBrief: In addition to Torah as an inheritance and the command to prepare oneself to learn Torah, Torah is also called a gift, which is a level above even the aspect of preparing oneself.

translations.translation: And behold, in addition to the two matters mentioned above regarding Torah
(the inheritance of Torah,
and "prepare yourself to learn Torah"),
Torah is also called by the name "gift".
As in the wording of the blessing over the Torah: "and He gave us His Torah," and we conclude "Who gives the Torah,"
and the holiday of Shavuos is called
"the time of the giving of our Torah."
For the matter of the gift in Torah is above even the aspect of "prepare yourself to learn Torah."
And the explanation is,
that the difference between dew and rain is,
that the descent of rain depends on the work of man
(as it is written,
"And it will be, if you surely listen...")
(and then
"I will give the rain of your land..."),
but dew does not depend on the work of man
(as our sages said,
"Dew is not withheld"),
and so it is in spirituality,
that rain is the drawing down that comes through an arousal from below, and dew is the drawing down from Above, from its own accord.
And from this it is understood,
that what was explained above, that the aspect of the dew of Torah is the drawing down of Torah as it is Above, through engaging in Torah for its own sake
("Whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him"),
is in general,
but in particular,
even the drawing down of Torah as it is Above,
"the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews,"
since the drawing down is through man reading and reviewing,
it is included in the aspect of the rain of Torah,
and the aspect of the dew of Torah is a more elevated level in Torah,
which is not drawn down through man's engagement in Torah
(not even through engaging in Torah for its own sake),
and its drawing down is from its own accord.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The Sages' statement that the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah during the first three hours refers to the dew of Torah, a drawing down from Above that is independent of man's arousal, rooted in the first three of Atik.

translations.translation: And this is what our sages said,
"During the first three hours, the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah,"
and the precise point in this is known,
for "whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,"
and since Israel engages in Torah throughout the entire day
(one learns at this hour and another learns at that hour),
then the Holy One, blessed be He, also engages in Torah throughout the entire day,
and nevertheless they said that during the first three hours the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah.
And the point of the explanation in this is,
that this matter of "whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him" is a drawing down from Above that comes through an arousal from below
(man's engagement in Torah),
and therefore,
the drawing down is according to the measure of the arousal from below.
For this is what they said, "whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,"
that this that the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews is "opposite him,"
according to the measure of man's study.
And this, that during the first three hours the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah, is a drawing down from Above from its own accord,
from a place that arousal from below does not reach there.
And this matter is the aspect of the dew of Torah,
for the root of dew is in the first three of Atik.
And this is the connection of "the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah"
(the dew of Torah)
to the first three hours,
for the first three
[hours]
are the first three of Atik.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Within the inner dimension of Torah there is an external and internal aspect; the revealed part deals with the order of spiritual descent and is attainable through study for its own sake, while the essential aspect is the delight of Torah beyond comprehension, corresponding to the gift of Torah.

translations.translation: And this can be explained based on what is known,
that even in the inner dimension of Torah there is an external aspect and an internal aspect.
For that which the inner dimension of Torah speaks about matters of the chain of descent is its revealed aspect.
[And it is similar to the revealed dimension of Torah, which speaks about worldly matters.
Except that the revealed dimension of Torah speaks about physical matters,
and the inner dimension of Torah speaks about spiritual matters.]
And this level within the inner dimension of Torah is in the category of comprehension.
But the essential matter of the inner dimension of Torah is that Torah is the delight of the Above,
a delight that is beyond comprehension.
And it can be said,
that the drawing down of the inner dimension of Torah through engaging in Torah for its own sake,
about which they said "whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him"
[the matter of "prepare yourself to learn Torah"],
is the revealed aspect of the inner dimension of Torah,
which speaks about matters of the chain of descent and the like.
And the drawing down of the inner dimension of Torah from its own accord,
about which they said "during the first three hours the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah"
[the matter of the gift of Torah]
is the aspect of the delight of Torah that is beyond comprehension.
